why_this_file_exists: An R-35 verifier noticed that oracle-campaign-close-leaf0.json carries an `asides_flagged_not_part_of_the_verdict` block asserting two defects in CACHED DATA, and that the commit body landing that receipt never mentioned it and filed no follow-up. Both claims were re-verified here against data/ directly, and both hold. They are filed as dated, gated entries rather than left inside an oracle receipt's aside, because an aside inside a receipt about something else is prose nobody re-reads -- which is the shape this campaign exists to end. Neither reaches a damage number: rule 5 keeps every runtime item value in item_effects.py, and neither consumer below is on a serving path. They are real defects in evidence assets, and they are the kind that becomes a wrong number the first time somebody sums the wrong field.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves from defects[] to retired[] only when the contradiction is resolved in the cached data or its producer, and only together with its gate test's own inversion: the reproducer stops reproducing and the test asserts the resolved property instead. Deleting an entry is not closing it. Note that data/ is refreshed by scripts/patch_update.py from the wiki, so entry 1 closes when the upstream text is right or when the consumer stops trusting the field, not by editing the cache in place.
how_an_entry_is_scheduled: Added 2026-08-17, and the finding is a certification reviewer's: both entries were correctly outside the campaign's scope and were therefore unowned work with no scheduled home -- filed, gated, and waiting for nobody in particular. A gap with a blocker but no home is the shape a defect rots in, so every open entry now names one, and a home here is a ROUTE that already exists rather than a promise somebody will remember. The route is patch day, and it is the honest one for both: scripts/patch_update.py is the only writer of data/ (CLAUDE.md rule 2), its rebuild step regenerates build_effect_catalog.py and build_receipts.py -- which are exactly the two consumers these entries name -- and it is therefore the one moment when the person holding the lever is looking at the asset. What the schedule adds is that the run SAYS SO: print_audit() prints one line per open entry, read from this file, so a patch-day operator is told what is waiting on the pull instead of being expected to have read a receipt. The scheduling claim is asserted in both directions by the gate -- every open entry names a home, and the named route really reads this artifact -- because a home nothing consumes is the declaration this campaign spent its length removing. Scheduling is not fixing: both entries stay OPEN, gap G11 stays OPEN, and what changes is that the work has an owner-shaped moment rather than none.

defects.raised_by: an aside in oracle-campaign-close-leaf0.json, re-verified against data/items.json by the remediation lane for slice group campaign-close
defects.what: data/items.json['4005'].simpleDescription reads 'Defer damage until later.' Imperial Mandate defers nothing. Its two cached passives are Control -- immobilizing abilities have their cooldown reduced equivalent to 20 ability haste -- and Command -- immobilizing a champion marks them Vulnerable for 4 seconds, increasing damage taken by 7%.
defects.why_it_matters: scripts/build_effect_catalog.py::_text puts simpleDescription FIRST in the string its tag derivation runs over, ahead of every passive's own text. So the catalog entry for the campaign's headline item opens with a sentence about a mechanic the item does not have, and any tag keyed on that wording is keyed on another item's behaviour.
defects.why_it_does_not_move_a_number: No src/ module reads simpleDescription; the effect catalog is a front-end asset. Rule 5 requires every runtime item value to come from item_effects.py typed accessors.
defects.reproducer: json.load(open('data/items.json'))['4005']['simpleDescription'] == 'Defer damage until later.', while item_source.effect_text over its two passives mentions neither deferral nor delay.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: the field describes one of the item's own cached passives, or the catalog stops reading it.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: data/ is a cache with one writer. CLAUDE.md rule 2 routes every data update through data_updater.py from the wiki, so hand-editing the cached field would make the next patch-day pull silently revert it -- a fix that un-fixes itself is worse than a filed defect. The choices are an upstream correction or a consumer that stops trusting the field, and the second is a change to what the catalog means.

scheduled_home.what_fires_it: The next wiki re-pull. Patch day is the only act that rewrites the cached text this entry is about, and its rebuild step re-runs scripts/build_effect_catalog.py -- the consumer whose _text puts simpleDescription first -- so the defect and the asset it corrupts are regenerated in the same run. print_audit() now prints this entry, so the operator is told rather than expected to remember.
scheduled_home.how_it_closes_from_there: Either the pulled text describes one of the item's own passives, in which case the reproducer in tests/test_escalated_defects_cached_data.py goes red and the entry is retired with its assertion inverted; or the operator decides the catalog stops trusting the field, which is a change to what the catalog means and is that slice's to scope. Both decisions are taken while looking at freshly pulled data, which is why this is the route and not a backlog.

defects.raised_by: an aside in oracle-campaign-close-leaf0.json, re-verified against data/atoms/items.json by the remediation lane for slice group campaign-close
defects.what: Imperial Mandate's Control passive states ONE fact: 'Abilities with immobilizing effects have their cooldown reduced equivalent to 20 ability haste.' data/atoms/items.json['objects']['4005'] turns that single branch into three atoms, all sourced to passives[0].branches[0] and all valued 20.0: control.immobilize, stat.haste and timing.cooldown.
defects.why_it_matters: Two of the three are wrong about what 20 is. control.immobilize reads as an immobilize magnitude and is a haste figure; stat.haste reads as a flat stat and is a CONDITIONAL cooldown reduction that applies only to immobilizing abilities -- while the item's real flat stat, stats.abilityHaste, is 15. A consumer summing stat.haste over an item's atoms overstates Imperial Mandate by 20 ability haste, and one reading control.immobilize as a magnitude reads a number that is not one.
defects.why_it_does_not_move_a_number: data/atoms/ feeds scripts/build_receipts.py, which reads atom_id namespaces to build evidence packets, and no src/ runtime module reads it. The overstatement is available, not taken.
defects.reproducer: The atom rows for object 4005 include control.immobilize, stat.haste and timing.cooldown, each valued [20.0], each with source 'Imperial Mandate.passives[0].branches[0]', while stats.abilityHaste.flat is 15.0.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: one branch yields at most one atom per distinct fact, and a conditional cooldown reduction is not spelled as a flat stat.
defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: The fix is in scripts/atomize.py's keyword extraction, which fans one branch out across every keyword it matches with no arbitration between them. Changing that arbitration re-atomizes every item in the corpus and moves data/atoms/items.json, which is an evidence asset with its own manifest and hashes -- a slice with its own occurrence line, not a line in a remediation commit whose subject is something else.

scheduled_home.what_fires_it: The same run, for a different reason: the fix is a scripts/atomize.py arbitration slice that re-atomizes the whole corpus, and patch day's rebuild step already re-runs scripts/build_receipts.py over the unified Atomizer item domain -- the one consumer this entry names. A corpus-wide re-atomization landing on the day the corpus is rebuilt anyway is one moved asset instead of two, which is the whole of why the slice is scheduled here rather than run against a quiet tree.
scheduled_home.how_it_closes_from_there: The arbitration slice carries its own Expected qualifying occurrences line, as this entry's why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it already says it must, and it retires this entry by inverting the reproducer: one branch yields at most one atom per distinct fact, and a conditional cooldown reduction is not spelled as a flat stat. Naming the route does not scope the slice and does not shrink it.
